messages:
sam: Heads-up — playing with a new runway forecast card for the cost console. Idea: show 7/30-day projected token burn per-product if current throttle/prefetch mix holds. Quick sketch: https://figma.redwood/runway-forecast (very rough).

jia: Love the idea. Two quick Qs: (1) are we doing this at tenant-level only or per-route too? (2) how do we account for cache-prefetch savings vs hotpath tokens — needs to be defensible for chargebacks.

sam: Pref route + tenant. The tricky bit is attributing prefetch wins: proposal is to show an amortized prefetch line that spreads estimated savings across recent warmups. Basically: credit = prefetch_savings / warmup_window_seconds.

hector: Hmm. Amortized works for visuals but ops needs exact ledger numbers for billing. Might confuse customers if the dashboard shows a negative runway but invoices differ. We need a toggle: UI-level amortized view vs raw ledger view.

olivia: Agree with hector. Also UX: add a smoothing window control (slider) so users can move between immediate spikes and smoothed runway. Default to 7d smooth. :sparkles:

jia: On attribution math — what about sampling bias? Our telemetry samples 10% of invocations for deep token traces. If we extrapolate, we need a confidence band. Can we add a 90% CI ribbon?

sam: Yes — add CI. Implementation thought: compute mean token burn per-sample, scale by invocations, then estimate variance and propagate. Might be noisy for low-traffic routes. Show a disabled tooltip for <100 samples/day.

hector: Routing policy interaction: if runway shows a looming spike, can we surface recommended actions? e.g., suggest switching route to cheaper model variant or increasing batch size. Not prescriptive but a checklist.

jia: That ties into rollout UX: show canary impact preview — if you route 20% to small-quantized model, runway shifts X%. We need a simulator API behind the card: /internal/simulate_runway?route=...&split=0.2&model=...

ops-bot: [deploy-bot] Simulation API deployed to staging at https://staging.api.redwood/simulate_runway (v1). Response shape is sampled; beware of missing prefetch rows.

olivia: Nice. For the console widget, propose three panes: (1) runway chart + ribbon CI, (2) action suggestions (routing/quantize/batching), (3) audit trail for how prefetch amortization was computed. Keep the audit condensed but link to full math.

sam: UX nit: action suggestions should be gated by user perms (only platform admins see routing toggles). Also show estimated delta in $/day and latency change. Keep the default in tokens, with dollar conversion toggle.

jia: Backend concern: we currently compute token-level cost in the econ-agg pipeline once an hour. For real-time preview we'll need a fast stream aggregate or a cached rolling window. Either: (a) add a 1m-resolution aggregator that stores per-route deltas, or (b) accept a 15m latency for runway. Which do we prefer?

hector: Ops preference: 1m aggregator but sample-tier for low-traffic routes to save storage. Implement via downsampling policy: >100req/min get 1m resolution, else 15m. Should be configurable.

sam: Sounds good. Implementation tasks: frontend prototype (olivia), simulation API polish (jia + eng-platform), 1m aggregator PR (hector + eng-infra), add CI ribbon math doc (sam). I'll open a GH issue and assign.

olivia: I'll mock states for low confidence and billing-discrepancy (tooltip explaining amortized vs ledger).

jia: I'll add endpoint auth + perf tests. Also we should add unit tests for extrapolation with edge cases (zero prefetch, sustained warmups).

hector: One more ask — for internal billing we should log the raw components used to compute the amortized line: raw_tokens, prefetch_hits, warmup_count, sample_rate. Make it easy to reconcile.

sam: Agreed. Ok everyone, I'll file the issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/issues/12345 and tag y'all. Thanks! :raised_hands:
